title: PM to participate in Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme on 15 November
subtitle:
Programme marks the 151st Birth Anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda


PM to inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of development projects worth around ₹3,000 crore


Projects aimed towards tribal empowerment with focus on strengthening education, healthcare, livelihoods, preservation of tribal heritage and community infrastructure


PM to also inaugurate Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighter Museum in Mizoram
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 4:11PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will participate in the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra on 15th November 2026 at 11 AM via video conferencing. He will also address the gathering on the occasion of the 151st Birth Anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda.
During the programme, Prime Minister will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of 246 development projects worth around ₹3,000 crore. These projects are aimed at strengthening education, healthcare, livelihoods and community infrastructure for tribal communities across the country.
Prime Minister will inaugurate 173 projects, including 38 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) for tribal students and 100 Multi-Purpose Centres under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), which will serve as hubs for service delivery and community activities. He will also inaugurate various other projects under PM-JANMAN and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA).
Other key projects to be inaugurated include the Tribal Research Institute (TRI) building at Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh, and the Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighter Museum at Aizawl, Mizoram, aimed at preserving tribal culture and heritage. The museum commemorates the courage, valour and sacrifices of Mizo tribal freedom fighters, while showcasing the rich cultural traditions, historical legacy and heritage of the Mizo people. It is named after Ropuiliani, a nineteenth-century Mizo chieftainess who courageously resisted British colonial rule and is remembered as a symbol of tribal resistance and sacrifice.
Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of 19 new Eklavya Model Residential Schools, further strengthening the commitment to providing quality education to tribal children. He will also lay the foundation stone of 12 Tribal Multipurpose Marketing Centres (TMMCs) to strengthen market access for tribal producers. In addition, Prime Minister will also lay the foundation stone for 42 other projects under PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA.
The programme will mark the culmination of Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada, being observed across the country from 1st to 15th November 2026. During the Pakhwada, a range of national and grassroots-level programmes have been organised, including the President's interaction with EMRS students, the National Tribal Literary Festival, training programmes for tribal healers, health and nutrition camps for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), and community service drives in tribal villages under the Dharti Aaba Janbhagidari Abhiyan.

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal to Visit Egypt from 15–16 November 2026
subtitle:
Shri Piyush Goyal to Co-Chair 7th India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee Meeting

Business Forum to Strengthen Bilateral Trade and Investment Ties

Indian Business Leaders and Start ups to participate in the India–Egypt Business Forum

India Egypt Start up Forum to Explore New Trade, Investment and Joint Venture Opportunities

Large business delegation comprising 130+ business leaders and Start-ups to accompany Commerce and Industry Ministry
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 10:54AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal will undertake an official visit to the Arab Republic of Egypt from 15 to 16 November 2026. The visit aims to further strengthen the longstanding India–Egypt partnership, with particular emphasis on expanding bilateral trade, promoting investment, enhancing industrial cooperation and strengthening business-to-business engagement.
India and Egypt share longstanding historical, civilizational and people-to-people ties, which have evolved into a multifaceted partnership encompassing political, economic, security and cultural cooperation. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India–Egypt relations have gained renewed momentum, culminating in the elevation of bilateral ties to a Strategic Partnership, with a shared commitment to enhanced cooperation, including in the economic field.
The visit will comprise the 7th Session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC), the India–Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC) Meeting and the India–Egypt Business Forum. The programme will also include bilateral meetings with senior Egyptian Ministers, interactions with leading business representatives and meetings with the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), the Egyptian Junior Businessmen Association and the Egypt–India Startups Forum. These engagements are expected to provide fresh impetus to bilateral trade, investment, industrial cooperation and innovation linkages.
The 7th Session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC) will be co-chaired by Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt H.E. Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh on 15 November 2026 in Cairo.
The JTC has been elevated to the Ministerial level, reflecting the importance both countries attach to strengthening their economic and commercial partnership. The meeting will provide an opportunity to review the progress of bilateral trade and investment relations and discuss measures to further diversify and expand the bilateral trade basket. Discussions are expected to cover market access issues, non-tariff barriers, trade remedies, agricultural and food products, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, engineering goods, chemicals and petrochemicals, fertilisers, textiles, MSMEs, customs cooperation, services, renewable energy, green hydrogen, transport and logistics, among other areas of mutual interest.
Bilateral merchandise trade during April–September 2026 stood at USD 5.04 billion, registering a growth of 64 per cent over the corresponding period of the previous year. India's exports to Egypt during FY 2025–26 amounted to USD 3.87 billion, while imports from Egypt stood at USD 2.60 billion. India's major exports to Egypt include meat and poultry products, petroleum products, organic chemicals, cotton and machinery, while its major imports include crude petroleum, fertilisers, cotton and mineral products. (Source: DGCIS)
The two sides are also expected to discuss measures to facilitate greater participation of businesses in each other's markets, strengthen institutional mechanisms, address trade-related concerns and promote investment partnerships. Opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, and regional value chains are also expected to feature in the discussions. Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe.
A high-level Indian business delegation comprising over 130 CEOs and senior industry representatives from diverse sectors will participate in the India–Egypt Joint Business Council Meeting and the India–Egypt Business Forum. The JBC Meeting and Business Forum will provide platforms for direct engagement between business leaders and industry stakeholders from both countries to explore opportunities for enhancing bilateral trade and investment, fostering joint ventures, promoting technology partnerships and strengthening industrial collaboration.
During the visit, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal will also hold bilateral meetings with senior Egyptian Ministers to exchange views on further strengthening bilateral economic and commercial relations, particularly in the areas of trade, investment and industrial cooperation.
The visit reflects India's continued commitment to strengthening its economic engagement with Egypt, an important partner in North Africa and a strategic gateway to regional markets. Both countries have significant opportunities to expand cooperation in manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, automobiles, textiles, chemicals, engineering goods, food processing, renewable energy, logistics and emerging technologies. The visit is expected to provide fresh momentum to the India–Egypt economic partnership, strengthen institutional cooperation and create new opportunities for Indian and Egyptian businesses.

title: IICA Stakeholder Consultation held in New Delhi, experts emphasize Public Policy must Shift from ‘Control to Trust’
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), established under the aegis of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India, organised a high-level Stakeholder Consultation on ‘Public Policy & Corporate Affairs: Evolving Roles & Professional Development’ at the India Habitat Centre, New Delhi, recently.
The consultation was convened to define the scope of the public policy function within organisations, identify the capabilities its professionals require, and consider how learning pathways can be strengthened to meet both organisational expectations and national priorities.
Delivering the inaugural theme address,
Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, Director General & CEO, IICA
, underscored the need for continuous and meaningful dialogue between the public and private sectors. He placed the consultation within IICA’s wider mandate of building capacity across government and industry for better-informed engagement between the two. He observed that the way organisations understand policy, contribute to its development and use it to guide their decisions bears on the quality of governance and the wider business environment, and that the consultation was intended to identify practical ways of strengthening the skills this work demands.
The inaugural session had special addresses from retired senior beurocrats and corporate leaders like
Shri Amarjeet Sinha, IAS (Retd.), former Secretary, Government of India
, who called for collaborative governance and predictable policy, with business engaging the regulator before, during and after a policy shift. It is important to focus the systems thinking approach in the professional framework evolving in public policy function.
Dr. Anup K. Pujari, former Secretary, Government of India
, stressed the need to build the capacity of mid- and late-career professionals into a cadre able to bridge the public and private sides of the regulatory system.
Shri Arun Goyal, former Secretary, Government of India
, noted the growing part the private sector plays in the working of regulatory bodies and the development of regulation, which takes the function well beyond liaison.
Shri Rajiv Agarwal, IAS (Retd.),
Chief Corporate Affairs Officer, Tata Consultancy Services, emphasised communication and behavioural skills and the alignment of policy work with internal stakeholders and corporate strategy.
Shri Richard Rekhy, Vice Chairman, Grant Thornton Bharat
, said policy professionals need financial acumen and a view of national and global value chains to advise corporate leaders, with evidence as the basis of trust.
The deliberations that followed were organized in three tracks, (i) on the public policy and corporate affairs function, (ii) the evolving role of its professionals, and (iii) their education and professional development.
Participants examined the evolution of the function in business eco-system and how is it placed between the private sector and regulatory framework. They noted that twin tasks of the public policy function is to help the organisation understand what policy means for its strategy and of contributing credibly to policy discussions, the division of responsibility with legal, compliance and business teams, and how early it is brought into strategic business decisions.
The consultation also sketched the professional acumen for the public policy professionals of the country with the skills expected of practitioners at different career stages, among them a working knowledge of how governments and regulators take decisions, economic and data-based reasoning, and risk and stakeholder management, joined by the judgement to balance institutional priorities with the public interest. On capacity building, the conclusions favoured a multidisciplinary, case-based curriculum, flexible delivery suited to working professionals and internships with government.
The consultation drew 50+ senior representatives from listed and multinational companies, consulting and advisory firms, think tanks, industry associations, academia and civil society, along with senior government officials and policy researchers.
Setting the context,
Dr. Niraj Gupta, Head, School of Corporate Governance & Public Policy
, described the consultation as the start of a sustained effort by IICA to give this emerging profession an institutional anchor. He laid out the key questions for the consultation on emergence of public policy, and how capability can be built through education and practice. The consultation was coordinated by Mr. Manoj Singh, Chief Program Executive, IICA.
The deliberations concluded with a roadmap for IICA to work with industry bodies and academic institutions in support of this emerging profession, so that public policy professionals are equipped to work at the interface of corporate affairs and national development.
The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA) is a think tank under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India, dedicated to serving the corporate sector through knowledge, governance, and transformation.

title: Consent Manager Registration Framework Comes into Effect; MeitY Secretary Launches Online Registration Portal
subtitle:
Eligible Indian Companies Can Now Apply For Registration As Consent Managers Through dpbi.gov.in; Minimum Net Worth
Requirement Set At ₹2 Crore
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 12:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The registration framework for Consent Managers under the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, came into effect on 13 November 2026. As part of this phase of implementation, Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), launched the online portal
https://dpbi.gov.in
to enable eligible companies to apply for registration as Consent Managers.
The framework marks an important step towards operationalising a system that enables Data Principals to exercise greater control over consent relating to their personal data. It forms part of the phased implementation of the DPDP framework and enables eligible entities to seek registration and prepare to offer consent management services.
Role and Accountability of Consent Managers
A Consent Manager is an entity registered with the Data Protection Board of India (Board) that enables Data Principals to give, manage, review and withdraw consent through an accessible, transparent and interoperable platform. The framework seeks to strengthen trust and accountability in the digital ecosystem, with Consent Managers being accountable to the Data Principals.
Eligibility and Registration Process
Companies incorporated in India with adequate technical, operational and financial capacity, including a net worth of not less than ₹2 crore, may seek registration as Consent Managers. These requirements are intended to ensure that registered entities have the resources and capabilities to provide secure, reliable and accountable services.
Eligible companies may apply to the Board for registration through the newly launched portal. The Board will assess applications against the applicable requirements and may register qualifying companies. The list of registered Consent Managers will be made publicly available on the Board’s website.
Other key provisions concerning the rights of Data Principals, the obligations of Data Fiduciaries, and the Board’s inquiry and penalty processes are scheduled to come into effect on 13 May 2027.
Further information on the DPDP Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025 is available on the Ministry’s website at
https://www.meity.gov.in/
. For related queries, the email address

title: Union Environment Minister reviews Measures to Intensify Action against Air Pollution in Delhi-NCR
subtitle: NCR States need to Move beyond Planning and ensure Strict, Time-bound and Coordinated Ground-level Enforcement: Shri Bhupender Yadav
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 1:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today chaired a review meeting to assess measures undertaken by Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan for mitigation of air pollution in Delhi-NCR. The Minister has held more than 30 review meetings with NCR State Governments, Municipal Bodies over the past one year to strengthen air pollution preparedness and ensure effective implementation of control measures already identified in the detailed action plans prepared under Shri Yadav's guidance.
State Environment Ministers, Sardar Manjinder Singh Sirsa (NCT Delhi); Shri Rao Narbir Singh (Haryana); and, Shri Arun Kumar Saxena (Uttar Pradesh) joined the meeting virtually. Shri Narendra Bhooshan, Secretary (MoEFCC) and Dr. Amandeep Garg, AS (MoEFCC) and Chairman (CPCB) joined the meeting virtually from Antalya, Türkiye. Shri Tarun Pithode, Member Secretary, CAQM, presented the progress made by NCR States, while Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, CAQM, gave an overview on the on-ground implementation of the action plans of different States and measures yet to be taken on different fronts.
With winter pollution intensifying, the Union Minister directed all agencies to move beyond planning and ensure rigorous, time-bound and coordinated enforcement on the ground. Emphasising that air pollution does not recognise State boundaries, he called for coordinated implementation of matching pollution control measures across NCR. Shri Yadav also stressed real-time monitoring through Integrated Command and Control Centres (ICCCs) and direct accountability of field officers for violations. State Governments were directed to nominate Secretary level officials for 7 cities in Haryana, 4 cities in UP and 4 cities in Rajasthan for making them responsible for implementation of pollution control measures through field visits and report to CAQM on weekly basis. CAQM was requested to issue notices to non-performing officers.
Shri Yadav further emphasized that all concerned States must install ANPR cameras, failing which CAQM would initiate criminal prosecution against delinquent Transport Department officials after 30.11.2026. The CPCB was directed to immediately seal the identified 191 non-conforming polluting industries, which despite repeated directions had not even placed orders for installation of Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs). To ensure immediate corrective action, regular review of respective hotspot action plans of individual States would be undertaken by the Secretary (MoEFCC), Secretary (MoHUA), Chairman (CPCB), and Chairperson, CAQM, along with other senior officers. The Union Environment Minister, along with the concerned State Ministers, would also undertake regular field inspections, Shri Yadav stated.
Issue-wise detailed directions on various action points are given as follows:
Strict Enforcement of GRAP and Winter Action Plans:
The Minister directed all agencies to ensure strict implementation of GRAP and called upon NCR States to adopt Delhi's hotspot-focused winter action plan, covering traffic management, work-from-home measures, construction restrictions and prevention of open burning. In accordance with CAQM's order dated 30.10.2026, dust-generating Construction and Demolition (C&D) activities have been restricted across NCR from 5th to 20th November 2026.
Road Dust and Traffic Management:
Reviewing road dust management, Shri Yadav noted that only 3,221 km of the targeted 5,480 km of roads had been redeveloped. He directed road-owning agencies to prioritise pothole repairs, damaged footpaths, central verges and end-to-end paving as per CAQM framework, along with AI-based videographic surveys. Mechanical road sweeping machines must be fully utilised and operated in double shifts, with digital tracking and AI-based monitoring through ICCCs. States were also directed to intensify deep-cleaning drives and ensure removal of silt, C&D waste and municipal waste. For traffic decongestion, the Union Minister directed immediate action at the 233 identified congestion points across NCR and fresh assessments by respective States. MCD was asked to complete installation of Multi-Lane Free Flow systems at 154 Delhi border entry points by 31.12.2026.
Vehicular and Industrial Pollution:
On vehicular pollution, Shri Yadav called for expediting the PARIVARTAN Scheme for replacing pre-BS-VI trucks and buses with BS-VI, CNG and electric vehicles by 2028, particularly accelerating beneficiary registrations in Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Haryana by organizing PARIVARTAN Melas at State level immediately. The States were also asked to expedite installation of ANPR-based monitoring systems at fuel stations, integrated with VAHAN and PUCC databases, for intensified action against old and polluting vehicles.
On Industrial Emissions, the Minister noted that 2,298 of the 2,345 targeted industries (98%) had been connected to OCEMS, while the remaining 47 units had been closed or sealed. He called for strict enforcement of the 50 mg/Nm³ particulate matter emission norm, with non-compliant industries facing closure, electricity disconnection and sealing wherever required.  He noted that under the CPCB's winter enforcement SOP, effective from 01.10.2026 to 28.02.2027, OCEMS-based alerts and monitoring cells have been operationalised across NCR. State Pollution Control Boards were asked to facilitate MSMEs in accessing financial assistance under the Swachh Pawan Neel Gagan, Swasth NCR (SPNG-NCR) Scheme for installation of APCDs and take action against the non-compliant polluting industries in non-conforming areas.
Waste Management and Prevention of Open Burning:
The Union Minister stressed on the States to bridge the 6,747 TPD gap in municipal solid waste processing capacity, strictly prevent open dumping and burning, and expedite remediation of legacy waste at Okhla, Ghazipur, Bhalswa and Bandhwari. He also called for physical inspection of over 3,000 active C&D sites, timely lifting of waste from secondary collection points, ensuring functional recycling plants and digital tracking of waste from collection to processing through ICCCs. Municipal bodies, RWAs and private establishments were asked to provide non-polluting heating alternatives for security and sanitation staff, with ward-level officers and sanitation inspectors made responsible for surveillance and prevention of open burning.
Hotspot Management:
Highlighting the need for targeted interventions, Shri Yadav emphasized that all NCR States must identify pollution hotspots in major cities and prepare focused Hotspot Action Plans, particularly covering markets, schools, hospitals, railway stations and bus terminals.
Technology-driven Monitoring and Public Participation:
Emphasising technology-led enforcement, the Minister highlighted Delhi's ICCC, launched on 05.10.2026, and CAQM's PAVAN (Platform for Air Quality Vigilance and Analytics for NCR), which integrates air quality, emissions, meteorological, satellite and compliance data on a single platform. Shri Yadav stressed that real-time inputs from sensors, cameras and satellites must be used alongside physical inspections to identify violations and ensure swift enforcement. Shri Yadav also called upon all NCR States and agencies to ensure time-bound completion of pending actions and undertake extensive Information, Education and Communication (IEC) campaigns involving citizens, RWAs, transport associations and the construction industry.
Concluding the review, the Union Minister emphasised that coordinated efforts, field-level accountability and visible action on the ground are essential to effectively address the challenge of air pollution in Delhi-NCR.

title: DRI seizes 20 kg meth tablets hidden in specially fabricated cavity of tipper truck in Assam; one arrested

content:
Continuing its major crackdown on trafficking of contrabands in the North Eastern region of the country, officers of the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), in an intelligence led operation conducted jointly with the personnel of the 38 Battalion of Assam Rifles, seized 20 kg methamphetamine tablets (commonly known as yaba) from a tipper truck on 12th November 2026.
Acting on an intelligence input, DRI officers intercepted a Tata tipper truck near Borkhola in Cachar district and during its detailed inspection, with the assistance of a mechanic, officers detected a specially concealed cavity in the upper inner portion of the truck's right-side panel. The panel bore signs of cutting and welding, which had been camouflaged with cement and paint.
Upon opening the cavity, officers recovered
32 packets containing pinkish-orange tablets suspected to be methamphetamine
. The recovery comprised 17 brick-shaped packets weighing 1 kg each and 15 rectangular packets weighing 200 grams each. Preliminary field tests on representative samples using an NDPS Field Detection Kit indicated the presence of amphetamine.
The recovered tablets, weighing
20 kg in total
, along with the truck, were seized under the relevant provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. The occupant of the truck was arrested under the provisions of the Act.
The operation has exposed an innovative concealment method involving a fabricated cavity inside the side panel of a tipper truck, with the opening camouflaged using cement and paint to evade detection during routine checks.
DRI remains committed to dismantling drug trafficking networks and curbing the flow of illicit narcotics through sustained intelligence-led operations and inter-agency cooperation.

subtitle:

Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava Attends Inauguration of Health Pavilion at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi

Health Pavilion Themed ‘युवा भारत, स्वस्थ भारत’ Highlights Preventive Healthcare, Healthy Lifestyles and Youth Participation in Building a Healthier Nation

39 Stalls Representing 24 National Health Programmes and Organisations Showcase Government's Healthcare Initiatives, Achievements and Services

Interactive Activities, Live CPR Demonstrations, Health Awareness Sessions and Dedicated Kids’ Zone to Engage Visitors and Promote Healthy Living
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 2:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) is showcasing its flagship health programmes, key achievements and public healthcare initiatives through a dedicated Health Pavilion at the
45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026
, being organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from 14th to 27th November 2026.
The Health Pavilion was inaugurated today by Dr. M. Srinivas, Member, NITI Aayog, in the presence of Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Union Health Secretary; Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, Department of Health Research (DHR) and Director General, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Shri Sunil Kumar Barnwal, Chief Executive Officer, National Health Authority (NHA), and other senior officials of the Ministry.
The Ministry's participation in the prestigious annual event provides an important platform to connect directly with citizens, showcase the Government's wide-ranging healthcare initiatives and promote greater public awareness about preventive healthcare, early diagnosis and healthier lifestyles.
‘
युवा भारत
,
स्वस्थ भारत’
:
Promoting a Culture of Preventive Healthcare
This year's Health Pavilion, themed ‘युवा भारत, स्वस्थ भारत’, places special emphasis on preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyle practices and the active involvement of young people in building a healthier and more resilient India.
The theme reflects the importance of encouraging healthy habits from an early age, strengthening health awareness and empowering citizens to make informed choices about their physical and mental well-being.
Through informative exhibits, interactive demonstrations and public engagement activities, the Pavilion seeks to make healthcare information accessible, relatable and engaging, particularly for youth, children and families.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. M. Srinivas highlighted the increasing burden of Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) and lifestyle-related health conditions, underscoring the need for a stronger focus on preventive healthcare and the adoption of healthier lifestyle practices.
He emphasised the importance of public awareness, early detection and timely medical intervention in preventing and managing NCDs, while encouraging citizens to take greater responsibility for their health through informed lifestyle choices.
Dr. Srinivas observed that the Health Pavilion offers a valuable opportunity for citizens to learn about common health risks, understand preventive measures and familiarise themselves with various Government healthcare programmes and services.
He encouraged visitors, particularly young people and families, to actively participate in the Pavilion's activities and use the opportunity to enhance their understanding of health and well-being.
Union Health Ministry Brings 24 Health Programmes and Organisations Under One Roof
The Health Pavilion brings together 24 National Health Programmes, Programme Divisions and participating organisations, represented through 39 stalls spread across 989 square metres on the Ground Floor of Hall No. 4 at Bharat Mandapam.
The Pavilion offers visitors a comprehensive overview of India's public healthcare initiatives, covering primary healthcare, disease prevention and control, immunisation, maternal and child health, digital health services, mental healthcare, food safety, organ donation and other important areas of public health.
Flagship initiatives and services being showcased include Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, Ayushman Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana through the National Health Authority, eSanjeevani, the Universal Immunisation Programme, Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram, TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, Tele-MANAS and several national disease prevention and control programmes.
The Pavilion also facilitates direct engagement between visitors and representatives of the Ministry's Programme Divisions and participating organisations, enabling citizens to learn about healthcare services, seek information and develop a better understanding of Government health initiatives.
Interactive Activities to Make Health Awareness Engaging and Accessible
A wide range of informative and participatory activities has been organised throughout the Pavilion to encourage public engagement and promote awareness about preventive healthcare.
These include live Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) demonstrations, health awareness sessions, Nukkad Natak, health talk shows and interactive quiz programmes.
The activities are designed to communicate important public health messages in simple and engaging ways, while enhancing awareness about disease prevention, early detection, emergency response and healthy lifestyle practices.
Dedicated Kids’ Zone Encourages Screen-Free Learning and Healthy Recreation
A special Kids’ Zone has also been established at the Health Pavilion, featuring traditional games and recreational activities for children.
With an emphasis on largely screen-free engagement, the zone seeks to encourage physical activity, social interaction and learning through play.
The initiative aims to familiarise children with the importance of healthy habits while providing an enjoyable and engaging environment for families visiting the Pavilion.
Special Focus on TB Awareness, Screening and Community Participation
A dedicated TB stall has been established to raise awareness about tuberculosis and inform visitors about prevention, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment and the range of services available under the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP).
As part of the activities, TB screening is being conducted using AI-enabled handheld X-ray technology, while a Medical Officer is providing medical consultations and guidance to visitors.
The stall is also facilitating the registration of Ni-kshay Mitras, encouraging individuals and organisations to support persons affected by TB, including through the provision of nutritional food baskets.
Public awareness activities, including Nukkad Natak, magic shows and interactions with the TB mascot, are being organised to communicate key messages on early detection, timely treatment, nutritional support and community participation in the fight against tuberculosis.
The initiative highlights the importance of collective action and citizen participation in advancing the goal of a TB-Mukt Bharat.
Strengthening Public Awareness and Citizen Participation for a Healthier India
The Health Pavilion at IITF 2026 reflects the Ministry's continued emphasis on bringing health information and public healthcare initiatives closer to citizens.
By combining informative exhibits, practical demonstrations, interactive activities and direct public engagement, the Pavilion seeks to encourage greater awareness about preventive healthcare and empower individuals and families to make healthier lifestyle choices.
The Ministry's participation also reinforces the importance of youth engagement, community participation and informed health choices in building a Swasth Bharat.

title: A journey through a divided homeland: Paweł Pawlikowski’s ‘Fatherland’ to mark the beginning of global cinematic celebrations in Goa
content:
Goa, 14 November 2026
Some journeys cross landscapes, while others travel through the complexities of memory, identity and belonging. Bringing together history and deeply personal relationships, Fatherland (Ojczyzna), directed by acclaimed Polish filmmaker Paweł Pawlikowski, has been selected as the Opening Film of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), setting the tone for nine days of cinematic celebration in Goa.
Set in the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, Fatherland explores the relationship between Nobel Prize-winning German writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, an actress, writer and rally driver. Returning to Germany after sixteen years of exile in the United States, Thomas Mann embarks on a challenging road trip with his daughter in a black Buick. Their journey takes them across a country devastated by war, from US-dominated Frankfurt to Weimar under Soviet control.
As father and daughter travel through a divided Germany, they encounter more than the visible scars of a nation torn apart by conflict. Their journey also brings them face to face with the deep divisions within their own family. Through this emotionally layered narrative, the film explores the intersections of personal relationships, history and the idea of home.
Featuring Sandra Hüller and Hanns Zischler in leading roles, the 82-minute drama is a collaborative production involving Poland, Germany, Italy and France. Presented in black and white, the film will have its India Premiere at the 57th IFFI.
Fatherland continues director Pawel Pawlikowski’s exploration of history and human relationships through an intimate narrative set against a significant moment in European history. The film has already travelled to major international festivals, including Cannes, San Sebastián and Telluride in 2026, earning Pawlikowski the Best Director Award at Cannes.
With Fatherland, the 57th IFFI begins its journey through stories that transcend geographical and cultural boundaries. As cinema brings together different worlds and perspectives, the opening film offers a fitting beginning to this year’s theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’.

title: BRICS Cinema takes centre stage at 57th IFFI with 21 films from across the world
subtitle: Showcase brings diverse cinematic narratives on democracy, freedom, identity, history and contemporary global concerns
content:
Goa, 14 November 2026
The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 will feature 'Films from BRICS', a showcase of cinema from BRICS countries that engages with questions of democracy, freedom, identity, history and contemporary global concerns. Drawing on histories, social realities and personal journeys, the films offer perspectives from the societies they emerge from.
Featuring 21 films, the selection moves across countries, languages and genres, bringing narratives that engage with questions of freedom, identity, social inequality, family, conflict, displacement and belonging. Several of these films look back at defining moments of struggle and change, from pro-democracy movements to the fight against slavery and colonial rule.
Brazil’s ‘
Amadeo and the Hypothetical New World
’ imagines an African inventor in 1830s Brazil whose invention becomes part of the struggle to liberate enslaved people. Indonesia’s ‘
The Sea Speaks His Name
’ follows the disappearance of a student activist during the country’s 1998 pro-democracy movement and his family’s search for answers. South Africa’s ‘
The Trek
’ takes viewers across the Kalahari Desert in the mid-19th century, confronting the brutality of the colonial frontier.
Contemporary concerns also find a place in the selection. ‘
Dreaming of Serenada
’, a Uganda-UK documentary, explores climate change through a father-daughter relationship and the impact of flooding on a rainforest landscape. ‘
Faya Dayi’
, from Ethiopia and the United States, examines communities connected to khat cultivation and consumption, bringing into focus livelihoods, social realities and the aspirations of young people. Iran’s ‘Poultry Farm’ follows an undocumented child from Iraq whose search for a missing friend puts his own life at risk.
Family, identity and personal choices form another strong theme. Saudi Arabia’s ‘Hijra’ follows a young girl, her grandmother and her missing sister on a journey that uncovers family secrets and generational differences. China’s ‘
Embers’
traces the consequences of a mix-up involving cremated ashes, bringing two women face to face with loss and mortality. ‘
The Condor Daughter’
, a Bolivia-Peru production, portrays a young woman from an indigenous Andean community torn between inherited musical traditions and her dream of becoming a performer. Nigeria-UK production ‘
Lady
’ follows a young taxi driver in Lagos whose encounter with a group of sex workers leads her towards solidarity and self-discovery.
The Indian entry, ‘
Article 370
’, directed by Aditya Dhar, is set against the backdrop of the 2016 Kashmir unrest and follows a mission to abrogate Article 370. The film received three honours at the 72nd National Film Awards in the categories of Best Film, Best Actress and Best Music.
The complete line-up also includes ‘
Kindik
(The Cord)’ (Kazakhstan), ‘
Baracoa
’ (Cuba and Italy), ‘
Bo Bo
’ (Russian Federation), ‘
Safe Exit’
(Egypt, Germany, Libya, Qatar and Tunisia), ‘
9 Temples to Heaven’
(Thailand, Singapore, France, Norway, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia and Qatar), ‘
Cotton
’ (Uzbekistan), ‘
Baga: Tomorrow Belongs to No One’
(Malaysia), ‘
1982
’ (Vietnam), ‘
And the Snow Was Falling’
(Belarus) and ‘
Baab
’ (United Arab Emirates).
Together, the 21 films offer audiences a cross-section of cinematic perspectives, with stories that move beyond national boundaries while engaging with shared questions of freedom, belonging, memory, resilience and change.
Scheduled from 20th-28th November 2026 across multiple venues in Goa, the 57th International Film Festival of India will showcase over 150 international films from 86 countries. title: ‘I Matter’: A Powerful Story of Identity, Belonging and Second Chances to be Screened as Mid-Fest Film at IFFI 2026
subtitle: Indian Premiere of Alina Șerban’s acclaimed film which won the Armani Beauty Audience Award at the Venice International Film Festival
content:
Goa, 14 November 2026
I Matter
(
Eu Contez
), a multilingual drama written and directed by acclaimed filmmaker Alina Șerban, will have its Indian Premiere as the Mid-Fest film at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). A co-production of Romania, Germany and Belgium, the 101-minute film explores identity, family, belonging and the pursuit of a future beyond the circumstances of one's past. Featuring dialogues in Romanian and Romani, the film brings a distinctive European cinematic perspective to the festival.
The film follows Rebeca, a young Roma woman preparing to leave the orphanage she has called home. With her father's impending release from prison, she hopes to find the family she has always longed for and begin a new chapter in her life. Her admission to university to study acting brings fresh hope and the possibility of shaping her own future. However, as she navigates an unfamiliar world, unresolved experiences from her past resurface, confronting her with difficult choices.
Through Rebeca's journey,
I Matter
explores the emotional challenges of growing up without a stable family environment, the search for acceptance and the determination to find one's place in society. Set against the experiences of a young Roma woman, the film also engages with questions of social inclusion, dignity and individual freedom.
The film marks the feature-directorial debut of Alina Șerban, an accomplished actress and playwright. A graduate of the National University of Theatre and Film in Bucharest, she has also trained at the Tisch School of the Arts, New York University, and the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, London. Her earlier works include
Alone at My Wedding
, which premiered at the Cannes Film Festival, and
Gipsy Queen
, for which she received several Best Actress honours. She also appeared in
Housekeeping for Beginners
, screened at the Venice Film Festival.
I Matter
premiered in the Venice Spotlight section of the 83rd Venice International Film Festival in September 2026, where it received the prestigious Armani Beauty Audience Award. The film stars Denisa Farcaș as Rebeca, alongside Sorin Mihai, Angelina Pavel, Vanessa Dancea, Raisa Mihai, Alexandru Stancu, Alina Berzunțeanu and Natalia Călin.
As the Mid-Fest presentation at IFFI 2026,
I Matter
will be screened simultaneously at 4:30 PM on November 24, 2026, at PVR INOX Panjim (Audi 1) and PVR INOX Porvorim (Audi 1). Director Alina Șerban and lead actress Denisa Farcaș will attend the festival as special guests. A red-carpet event featuring the film's guests is also scheduled at PVR INOX Panjim on the day of the screening.

title: First Regional Conference on Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 concludes in Tiruchirappalli, emphasising sustainable drinking water services and community ownership
subtitle: Five teams, led by senior officials, including Secretary DDWS and AS&MD NJJM, visit water supply infrastructure and participate in Jal Arpan Diwas celebrations across five villages
date:

                14 NOV 2026 3:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti
, today visited rural drinking water supply infrastructure and participated in the Jal Arpan Diwas celebration at Palamaneri Village in Tamil Nadu, as part of the second day of the Regional Conference on Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 held at Tiruchirappalli. The visit began at the historic Grand Anicut (Kallanai) on the Cauvery River, followed by field visit of the riverbed collector wells and headworks at Vadugakudi. At Palamaneri Village, the Secretary joined the community in celebrating, Jal Arpan Diwas, the formal handover of drinking water infrastructure to the Gram Panchayat, participated in a plantation activity and interacted with VWSC members, who shared how household tap connections had improved their daily lives. Women from the Sujalam Shakti Group also demonstrated water quality testing using Field Test Kits.
Reflecting on these experiences while addressing the concluding session of the Conference
, the Secretary emphasised that Jal Arpan should not be viewed merely as a ceremonial handover of infrastructure, but as the beginning of a sustained partnership between the State Government, implementing department and Gram Panchayat. He stressed that JJM 2.0 aims to move beyond providing household tap connections towards ensuring regular, reliable and safe drinking water services, with the long-term aspiration of 24×7 potable water supply directly from household taps. He also suggested that officials participating in Jal Arpan should drink water directly from village taps to strengthen community confidence in water quality.
The Secretary further emphasised that Gram Panchayats require continued technical support, handholding and capacity building to effectively manage drinking water services. He highlighted the importance of training elected Panchayat representatives and adapting training materials to local conditions. Referring to growing water stress, he urged States to utilise the Decision Support System (DSS) for planning rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge and other source sustainability measures. Appreciating the Government of Tamil Nadu for successfully organising the Conference, he encouraged participating States to continue exchanging experiences and learning from one another.
Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary and Mission Director,
National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), emphasised the importance of translating JJM 2.0 reforms into effective field-level implementation and strengthening coordination among concerned departments. During his visit to the village on the occasion of Jal Arpan Diwas, he personally drank water directly from a household tap, reinforcing community confidence in the quality and safety of the drinking water being supplied. He encouraged officials to adopt similar practices during field visits to build public trust in rural drinking water services. He further emphasised that Jal Arpan should be communicated as a step towards shared responsibility for sustainable water service delivery, rather than merely the handover of infrastructure. He also underscored the need to reassure Gram Panchayats of continued technical support from implementing departments, particularly for major repairs and infrastructure breakdowns, to strengthen their confidence in managing village water supply systems.
Shri D. Senthil Pandian, Joint Secretary, DDWS
, while summarising the two-day Conference deliberations, highlighted the systematic follow-up undertaken after the Departmental Summit held in September 2026. He informed that specific action points, responsible stakeholders and timelines had been identified, followed by inter-ministerial consultations with the Ministries of Panchayati Raj, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Tribal Affairs and Rural Development to strengthen convergence in financing, skilling, tribal drinking water coverage and source sustainability. Elaborating on the reforms under JJM 2.0, he emphasised institutional accountability, formal handover of infrastructure to Gram Panchayats, effective implementation of O&M policies, capacity building of VWSCs, dedicated District Technical Units, water quality monitoring, digital mapping through Sujalam Bharat and source sustainability planning using DSS. He urged States to adhere to their committed reform timelines ahead of the proposed national-level review in February 2027, with five Regional Conferences planned as part of the structured review process.
Shri Hari Narayanan M., Director, NJJM
, while proposing the Vote of Thanks, expressed gratitude to Secretary DDWS, Additional Secretary & Mission Director and Joint Secretary, NJJM, for their leadership and guidance. He appreciated the Government of Tamil Nadu, TWAD Board and other concerned departments for the excellent arrangements, and thanked participating States and Union Territories, Central Ministries, technical institutions, SPM-NIWAS and the NJJM team for their contributions towards making the Conference meaningful and productive.
Field Visits and Jal Arpan Diwas Celebrations
Earlier in the day, five teams led by senior officials, including Secretary DDWS, Additional Secretary & Mission Director NJJM, Joint Secretary DDWS, Director NJJM and Director SPM-NIWAS, along with representatives from participating States and Union Territories, visited rural drinking water supply infrastructure at Vadugakudi, Thiruchinampoondi, Thindukarai, Nochiyam and Keelaanbil headworks. The teams subsequently participated in Jal Arpan Diwas celebrations across five villages—Palamaneri, Ambedkar Nagar, Theeranmanagar, Ayyampalayam and Puthu Uthamanur, respectively, witnessing community participation and the formal handover of water supply infrastructure to Gram Panchayats.
The visits provided practical insights into source-to-tap drinking water infrastructure, including riverbed collector wells, pumping and distribution arrangements, and community-led operation and maintenance. Jal Arpan Diwas celebrations witnessed enthusiastic participation by Gram Panchayats, VWSC members, women's Self-Help Groups, schoolchildren and local communities. Activities included cultural performances, rangoli and painting competitions, demonstrations of water quality testing using Field Test Kits, community pledges, and the formal handing over of scheme documents and as-built drawings to Gram Panchayats.
During the subsequent debriefing session, representatives of all five teams shared their observations, highlighting innovative technical practices, women's participation in water quality surveillance, community ownership and the importance of sustainable O&M financing.
As part of the follow-up to the Departmental Summit held in September 2026 in the gracious presence of the Hon’ble Prime Minister, the first Regional Conference brought together seven participating States and Union Territories to exchange experiences, review progress on JJM 2.0 reforms and identify opportunities for convergence and collective action. On the first day,
Shri C. R. Paatil, Hon’ble Union Minister of Jal Shakti
, emphasised the need to accelerate the completion of remaining works and operationalise key structural reforms to ensure sustainable rural drinking water services. Deliberations involving Central Ministries, technical institutions and participating States/UTs focused on institutional strengthening, interdepartmental convergence, sustainable O&M financing, source sustainability, capacity building and Gram Panchayat-led water governance. The second day complemented these deliberations through field visits and Jal Arpan Diwas celebrations, providing practical insights into community ownership and sustainable management of rural drinking water systems.
The outcomes of the Conference, combining policy deliberations with field-level learning, are expected to strengthen interstate cooperation, accelerate implementation of JJM 2.0 reforms and facilitate the transition from infrastructure creation to sustainable, community-managed and reliable rural drinking water services.

title: Indian Railways Approves Weekly Train Service Connecting Janakpur Dham in Nepal with Ayodhya in India
subtitle: A Major Step Towards Strengthening Cross-border Connectivity, Religious Tourism and India-Nepal Friendship
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards strengthening India-Nepal connectivity, Indian Railways has approved the introduction of a new weekly train service between Janakpur Dham in Nepal and Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh, India.
The service will establish an important rail link between two destinations deeply associated with the Ramayana tradition – Janakpur Dham, revered as the birthplace of Mata Sita, and Ayodhya, the birthplace of Prabhu Shri Ram. The initiative will provide passengers from both countries with improved access to these prominent religious and cultural centres while reinforcing their shared civilizational heritage.
Connecting Key Destinations Across the Border
Covering approximately 604 kilometres, the weekly service will connect Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya Cantt., passing through several important towns and cities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.
The train will have commercial stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur and Ayodhya Dham, besides its terminal stations.
The service will operate once a week, with its originating days being Saturday from Janakpur Dham and Monday from Ayodhya Cantt.
Boost to Tourism, Trade and Regional Development
The new service is expected to make cross-border travel more convenient for pilgrims, tourists and other passengers. It will facilitate religious journeys between Janakpur and Ayodhya, encourage tourism circuits associated with the Ramayana and provide greater mobility to people travelling for education, business and family-related purposes.
Improved rail access is also expected to benefit local economies along the route by creating opportunities for tourism operators, hospitality establishments, local traders and traditional artisans. For communities in the border regions of Bihar and Nepal, the service will offer an additional passenger transport option and strengthen economic and social linkages.
Strengthening India-Nepal Friendship
India and Nepal share centuries-old cultural, historical and social bonds, with religious traditions and cross-border community relationships forming an integral part of this partnership. The new train service will add another dimension to bilateral cooperation by using railway connectivity to bring communities closer.
Through this initiative, Indian Railways continues to expand passenger connectivity while supporting regional tourism, economic activity and the enduring friendship between the two neighbouring countries.

title: Shivraj Singh Chouhan announces five lakh PMAY-G houses for Odisha
subtitle:
29 lakh women in Odisha become Lakhpati Didis; more support for women entrepreneurs

Every panchayat in Odisha to receive up to ₹2 crore for development

Balangir agriculture college to be developed as the country’s best institution

No eligible poor family in Odisha will be left without a pucca house

Solar-powered homes to help rural families cut bills and earn additional income

Women entrepreneurs to get loans without guarantees

Viksit Bharat–G RAM G scheme to accelerate rural development in Odisha
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 6:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today announced five lakh pucca houses for poor families in Odisha under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Gramin. Addressing a state-level program of the scheme in Balangir in the presence of Chief Minister Shri Mohan Charan Majhi. The program also witnessed the foundation stone laying for a new agriculture college in Balangir. Deputy Chief Minister and Agriculture Minister Shri Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo, Panchayati Raj and Drinking Water Minister Shri Ravi Narayan Nayak, Health and Family Welfare Minister Dr Mukesh Mahaling, Member of Parliament Smt Sangeeta Kumari Singh Deo, and local legislators Shri Naveen Kumar Jain, Shri Laxman Bag and Ms Rupa Mishra were among those present.
Shri Chouhan said that a fresh and proper survey had now been completed and no poor family would be left living in a kutcha house. All eligible families would receive pucca houses in a phased manner. He also announced that the Centre and the state government would jointly provide subsidies for installing solar panels on houses. This would help beneficiaries bring their electricity bills down to zero and earn additional income by selling surplus electricity.
29 lakh women become Lakhpati Didi in Odisha; ₹10 lakh crore credit initiative for women
Paying tribute to the strength and contribution of women, Shri Chouhan said that the Subhadra Yojana, under which women receive ₹10,000 annually, had strengthened their confidence and enhanced their dignity. He appreciated Odisha for achieving the target of 27 lakh Lakhpati Didis a year ahead of schedule, with 29 lakh women now having attained this status under the leadership of Chief Minister Shri Mohan Charan Majhi. The Union Minister said that, over the next five years, loans worth ₹10 lakh crore would be extended through banks to women across the country to help more women become Lakhpati Didis. He added that access to credit would no longer be limited to members of self-help groups. Women who wish to start their own businesses or livelihood activities individually would also be able to obtain loans without the requirement of a guarantee.
Balangir agriculture college to become the country’s leading institution; solar power to support farmers
Describing service to farmers as akin to worshipping God, Shri Chouhan assured that the new agriculture college in Balangir would be developed into the country’s finest agricultural institution with the support of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the Government of India. Leading agricultural scientists from across the country would work with farmers and help address their needs. He said that a comprehensive roadmap is being prepared in coordination with the Odisha government to modernise agriculture in the state. Under a proposed initiative, solar panels would be installed above agricultural fields, allowing farmers to cultivate fruits and vegetables beneath them. This would enable farmers to earn from both agriculture and solar power. Shri Chouhan also said that the names of eligible farmers who had been left out of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme had now been added to the beneficiary list.
Every panchayat to receive ₹1–2 crore for development; mafia networks dismantled
Outlining the government’s plans for rural development, Shri Chouhan said Odisha would receive approximately ₹4,000 crore this year under the Viksit Bharat–G RAM G scheme. This would provide every panchayat with ₹25 lakh to ₹50 lakh annually. Over five years, smaller panchayats would receive up to ₹1 crore and larger panchayats up to ₹2 crore for development works. The funds could be used to build roads, drains, schools and panchayat buildings, improve road connectivity to farmers’ fields and construct ponds for water conservation. He further said that, following the approval of 1,700 kilometres of roads under the fourth phase of the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, all remaining villages would also be connected through pucca roads.
‘Viksit Odisha’ vision rooted in the state’s culture and people
Paying tribute to Balangir’s rich cultural heritage, including its Nuakhai festival and Dalkhai and Rasarkeli dances, Shri Chouhan called upon the people to work together towards building a developed Odisha. Addressing the large gathering in his characteristic warm and personal style, he said he had not come as a distinguished guest or visitor, but as a humble public servant in his capacity as Minister for Agriculture and Rural Development. He said he saw Lord Jagannath in the living and vibrant people of Odisha and the image of Subhadra Maiya in the women of the state. Praising Chief Minister Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Shri Chouhan described him as a simple, approachable and dedicated public servant who worked tirelessly. He said that, with the objective of realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Viksit Bharat, the Chief Minister was working towards building a Viksit Odisha.

title: Dr. Jitendra Singh Celebrates World Diabetes Day with Enthusiastic Participation of Indian Diaspora in Italy; Highlights India's Scientific and Healthcare Progress
subtitle:
Minister calls for prevention of diabetes, particularly among youth – Stresses lifestyle modification and control of obesity

Minister says ‘Early Action on Diabetes’, the theme of World Diabetes Day, captures the essence of diabetes management through early detection, timely intervention and strict control of blood glucose levels
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 6:11PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union World Diabetes Day was observed in Rome with enthusiastic participation from members of the Indian diaspora in Italy, representing diverse sections of society, including students, women, entrepreneurs and professionals from different walks of life. The participants joined the programme with great enthusiasm and expressed happiness and pride over India’s remarkable progress in science, technology, research and healthcare during the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The gathering reflected the growing confidence of the Indian community in India’s scientific capabilities, healthcare initiatives and its expanding contribution to global scientific advancement.
The enthusiastic participation of the Indian diaspora, comprising students, women, entrepreneurs and members of the professional community, reflected the strong interest of Indians living abroad in India’s scientific and healthcare journey. The participants appreciated the country’s progress in scientific research, technological innovation and healthcare delivery under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, expressing pride in India’s growing global standing and its commitment to addressing important public health challenges such as diabetes.
Addressing the event organised at the Embassy of India in Rome on the occasion of World Diabetes Day, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, Dr. Jitendra Singh, a noted diabetologist and Professor, called for greater emphasis on the prevention of diabetes, particularly among young people, stressing that lifestyle modification, healthy dietary habits, physical activity and control of obesity remain the fundamental measures for tackling the growing burden of the disease.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that although several new groups of anti-diabetic drugs have emerged for the treatment of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, the basic mantra of diabetes management continues to be lifestyle modification and obesity control.
Referring to this year’s theme, ‘Early Action on Diabetes’, the Minister said it captures the entire spirit of the management strategies required to check the rapid spread of diabetes in society. He emphasised that proactive early detection and timely action, followed by strict control of blood glucose levels through both pharmaceutical and non-pharmaceutical measures, are essential to reducing the growing burden of diabetes.
Dr. Jitendra Singh expressed concern over the changing age profile of diabetes, noting that a disease previously associated largely with middle and old age is increasingly affecting young people in the prime of their lives. Diabetes at a younger age can have implications for an individual’s professional productivity and quality of life, while also requiring sustained attention to blood glucose control over a longer period to prevent damage to vital organs such as the kidneys, eyes and heart.
The Minister highlighted the close metabolic association between obesity, diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension and heart disease, stating that the Government of India has accorded priority to addressing these interconnected health concerns. He recalled that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has repeatedly emphasised the importance of controlling obesity.
Pointing to the particular vulnerability of Indians to central obesity, which is an independent risk factor for metabolic disorders, including diabetes mellitus, Dr. Jitendra Singh underlined the need to strengthen preventive healthcare and encourage healthier lifestyles.
The Minister also highlighted the integrated and holistic approach adopted by the Government of India since 2014 towards the management of metabolic disorders and lifestyle-related diseases. He referred to the establishment of the Ministry of Ayush, the introduction of wellness centres and the observance of the International Day of Yoga on June 21 every year, following the proposal of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, which was unanimously accepted by the United Nations. These initiatives, he said, contribute in different ways to reducing the burden of diabetes in society.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also referred to measures aimed at strengthening early detection and access to treatment, including provisions for mass screening for diabetes and initiatives under Ayushman Bharat to make healthcare more accessible and affordable.
Emphasising the importance of dietary discipline and physical activity, the Minister said that proper eating habits and an optimum level of physical activity are essential components of diabetes prevention and management. He also drew attention to physical and mental stress as contributing factors that require attention.
The Minister observed that India, with its large number of people living with diabetes, has considerable experience in managing the disease. Indian experts, he said, are well placed to share their experience and knowledge with counterparts in other countries and contribute to wider international efforts to address the challenge.
Dr. Jitendra Singh reiterated that the message of World Diabetes Day goes beyond treatment and calls for a stronger focus on prevention, early diagnosis and sustained management, particularly among the younger population.
The event was organised at the Embassy of India in Rome as part of the Minister’s official visit to Italy from November 11 to 15, 2026. The programme also included an interaction with members of the Indian community in Italy.

title: India commits over 7 million Euros as co-partner in Elettra 2.0 in Italy for development of next-generation synchrotron beamlines: Dr. Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
India to invest in advanced research infrastructure and human resource development over five years from 2026-27

Upgraded facilities to expand research opportunities in Chemistry, Physics, Advanced Materials and Structural Biology
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 3:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India has reaffirmed its commitment to advanced international scientific collaboration by announcing its participation as a co-partner in the redevelopment of research beamlines at Italy's Elettra Sincrotrone Trieste under the Elettra 2.0 programme, with an investment commitment of more than 7 million Euros over the next five years beginning 2026-27.
The announcement was made by Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, Dr. Jitendra Singh, during his visit to Elettra Sincrotrone Trieste on November 13, 2026. India's participation will support the development of research infrastructure and human resource capacity, marking a significant new phase in the longstanding scientific partnership between India and Italy.
The upgraded facilities will open new avenues for research in Chemistry, Physics, Advanced Materials, Structural Biology and other scientific areas, benefiting researchers from India as well as other countries.
India's participation in Elettra 2.0 builds on more than 25 years of scientific collaboration between Indian research groups and the Italian facility. Indian scientists have been conducting research experiments at Elettra since 1998 and continue to utilise its facilities. India is currently the second-largest user of Elettra after Italy, reflecting the sustained engagement of its scientific community with the facility.
The extent of this engagement is also evident from the more than 1,100 experimental proposals received by Elettra from Indian research groups. India ranks second in the number of proposals submitted, after Italy, which submitted 54,140 proposals, and ahead of France, with 1,098 proposals.
Under the Elettra 2.0 programme, the existing India-centric XRD2 and Xpress beamlines will be decommissioned and replaced by two new beamlines with enhanced capabilities. These will comprise a microfocus beamline for macromolecular crystallography, to be called micro-XRD (μXRD), and a beamline for high-pressure diffraction, to be called Xpress Superbend (Xpress-SB).
The redevelopment represents a continuation of India's earlier investment in dedicated research infrastructure at Elettra. The Department of Science and Technology (DST) had jointly supported the construction of the two existing sophisticated diffraction beamlines, XRD2 and XPRESS, with a contribution of approximately Rs. 22 crore, alongside the Italian side. Both beamlines were jointly inaugurated on October 20, 2016, during the visit of the Secretary, DST, to Italy.
Since their commissioning, these beamlines have been effectively utilised by Indian researchers, with approximately 50-60 Indian scientists visiting Trieste every year to conduct research experiments at the facility.
The Department of Science and Technology has also supported Indian researchers' access to Elettra through the Indo-Italian Executive Programme of Cooperation (EPOC). Under EPOC 2022-2024, DST sanctioned Rs. 2 crores over three years to support visits by 50 Indian researchers annually, with 25 visits in each semester, for conducting experiments against allocated shifts at Elettra beamlines.
The EPOC 2025-2027 also includes a proposal to support Indian researchers in conducting experiments at the facility, with a proposed allocation of Rs. 1.5 crore over three years.
DST had already conveyed its agreement to participate in the redevelopment of the India-centric beamlines under Elettra 2.0, and a Letter of Intent (LoI) had been signed in this regard. During the visit, India reaffirmed its commitment to the Elettra 2.0 initiative through the announcement of its investment commitment of more than 7 million Euros over five years.
The Indian participation will build upon the experience gained through the successful development and utilisation of the existing beamlines and support the creation of upgraded research infrastructure for the next phase of scientific collaboration between the two countries.
Through its participation in Elettra 2.0, India will continue to strengthen its engagement with the Italian research facility, while supporting expanded opportunities for Indian and international researchers in advanced and specialised areas of scientific research.

The Ministry’s pavilion, located at Hall No. 5, Ground Floor, ITPO, showcases the rich craftsmanship, traditional skills and entrepreneurial capabilities of artisans and beneficiaries associated with the Ministry’s Apex Corporations.
The participation reflects the Government’s continued commitment to promoting inclusive economic growth and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for disadvantaged and marginalized sections of society.
Guided by the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the principle of
‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’

A Senior Official in the Ministry informed that more than 130 artisans from 19 States are participating in this year’s edition through the Ministry’s three Apex Corporations namely National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).
He said the participating artisans are displaying an extensive range of handicrafts, handloom products, handmade articles and other traditional products, reflecting India's diverse cultural heritage and indigenous craftsmanship.
The initiative provides artisans with an important opportunity to connect with customers, explore new market opportunities, showcase their products to a wider audience and generate income through direct sales, he said.
The Official noted that by facilitating participation in prestigious national-level exhibitions and trade fairs, the Ministry is working towards strengthening market linkages, encouraging entrepreneurship and enabling beneficiaries to move towards greater economic self-reliance.

The Official said Hon’ble Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, launched the TULIP initiative recently during the Shilp Samagam Mela at Dilli Haat, in National Capital.  He said TULIP seeks to provide traditional artisans with an enhanced platform for showcasing and marketing their products.
The Official added the TULIP initiative aims to strengthen the visibility and market reach of artisan-made products at both national and international levels. It seeks to establish sustainable livelihood opportunities by connecting traditional craftsmanship with emerging market demands, while preserving and promoting India's rich artistic and cultural traditions, he said.
Through the brand, the Ministry endeavours to provide artisans with greater recognition, improved market access and opportunities to expand their entrepreneurial activities, the Official said.
The Official said the Ministry’s participation in IITF 2026 also underscores the importance of inclusive market development, where traditional skills and indigenous knowledge are linked with contemporary marketing opportunities.
The Ministry’s participation adds a social empowerment dimension to the event by bringing the products and entrepreneurial potential of artisans and beneficiaries from marginalised communities into the mainstream marketplace, he added.
The Official remarked that such platforms enable artisans from diverse social and geographical backgrounds to showcase their capabilities, strengthen their market presence and become active contributors to the country's economic development.
Through its continued efforts, the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment remains committed to advancing social and economic inclusion, promoting traditional artisanship, strengthening livelihood opportunities and ensuring that the benefits of development reach all sections of society, the Official concluded.
