title: MoU Between DoSJE and DGDE to Extend Senior Citizen Welfare Schemes to Cantonment Boards Across the Country
subtitle:
Union Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh and Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar to Witness Signing of MoU on November 16 Monday

New Day Care Centres, Senior Citizen Homes and Geriatric Caregiver Training to Strengthen Elderly Care Infrastructure
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 6:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE) under the  Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, will sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Directorate General Defence Estates (DGDE), Ministry of Defence, in the National Capital here on November 16 Monday.
The signing ceremony will take place in presence of the Hon’ble Raksha Mantri, Shri Rajnath Singh, and the Hon’ble Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar.
The MoU aims to establish a framework for cooperation, coordination and convergence between the two organisations for implementing senior citizen welfare schemes under the Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY) in Cantonment Boards across the country.
The partnership will leverage the infrastructure and administrative network of Cantonment Boards, along with the scheme support, financial assistance and technical expertise of the Department, to facilitate access to care, support and opportunities for active and dignified ageing.
The event will also be attended by Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; Smt. Shobha Gupta, Director General Defence Estates, and other senior officials of both the Ministries and departments.
Speaking about the initiative, Sajeesh Kumar N, Joint Secretary in the Ministry said the MoU represents a
Whole-Of-Government
approach towards the welfare of senior citizens. He said the well-established infrastructure and community-level presence of Cantonment Boards, in collaboration with the DGDE, will help extend senior citizen welfare services quickly to these areas.
The collaboration will also provide financial support for Senior Citizen Homes with residential facilities of 25/50-bed capacity, wherever feasible, to  help strengthen institutional care facilities and expand access to residential support for senior citizens, the Official said.
The official said the MoU builds on the momentum of the Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan, a national campaign on intergenerational bonding launched by the Ministry on November 4, 2026.
The participation of young people as trained caregivers and their engagement in activities promoting intergenerational relationships will contribute towards creating a supportive and inclusive environment for senior citizens, the Official said.
Shri Kumar N said the MoU will further promote intergenerational bonding through a pledge to be administered to students of schools run by Cantonment Boards, along with activities encouraging meaningful interaction between young people and the senior citizens.
He said the initiative seeks to foster respect and understanding between generations while recognising senior citizens as valuable sources of experience, wisdom and values.
The Official said India's population aged 60 years and above is projected to increase from approximately 10 Crore in 2011 to around 23 Crore by 2036. He said with changing family structures and increasing urbanisation, community-based facilities such as Day Care Centres and access to trained caregivers close to home are becoming increasingly important, he added.
The partnership with DGDE is expected to strengthen the availability of such services for senior citizens residing in Cantonment areas across the country, Shri Kumar N said.
Under the MoU, new Day Care Centres and related facilities for senior citizens will be established in Cantonment Boards under AVYAY, the Official said. Existing Day Care Centres being operated by Cantonment Boards will also be strengthened with support and assistance from the Department, he added.
Shri Kumar N said another key component of the partnership will be skill training for youth as geriatric caregivers through the training and channel partners of the Department which will contribute towards creating a trained workforce for elderly care while opening up new livelihood opportunities for young people.
The Official said that awareness camps will also be organised to disseminate information about the Ministry’s welfare schemes for senior citizens. Public representatives, prominent social workers and local communities will be mobilised to strengthen awareness and participation, he said.
Through this collaboration, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment continues its efforts to strengthen institutional support, expand community-based care facilities and promote the socio-economic well-being of senior citizens by enabling them to lead dignified, secure and self-reliant lives, Shri Kumar N remarked.
It is pertinent to mention that Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY) is the umbrella scheme of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment for the welfare of senior citizens. It aims to ensure that senior citizens lead healthy, happy, empowered, dignified and self-reliant lives. Its key components include the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens, Senior Citizen Homes, Geriatric Caregiver Training, the National Helpline for Senior Citizens (Elderline – 14567), Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana and other initiatives promoting active and healthy ageing.

title: National Tribal Literary Festival Concludes with Emphasis on Preserving Oral Traditions and Promoting Contemporary Tribal Literature
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 10:46AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The two-day National Tribal Literary Festival, organised by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs at the India Habitat Centre, New Delhi, concluded on 13 November 2026 with discussions on preserving India’s rich tribal literary traditions and connecting indigenous knowledge and oral narratives with contemporary literary expression. Organised as part of the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas celebrations, the festival brought together tribal writers, poets, researchers, linguists and scholars from across the country under the theme
‘From Oral Tradition to Contemporary Tribal Literature’
.
The concluding day featured thematic discussions on oral epics and heroic traditions, the contribution of indigenous knowledge to multilingual education, and readings by emerging tribal writers and poets. The sessions highlighted how stories, songs, epics and poetry continue to preserve the collective memory, cultural identity and lived experiences of tribal communities.
Oral Epics and Heroic Traditions
Moderated by Shri Prakash Jha, the first session featured Shri Bhagwandas Patel, Shri Upendra Anu and Shri Mayanglambam Sadanand Singh. The speakers explored the oral literary heritage of the Bhil and Gond communities, including
Gond Ramayana
and
Bhil Mahabharata
, as well as Manipur’s
Wari Leeba
storytelling tradition and the
Khamba-Thoibi
epic. The discussions highlighted the importance of documenting these traditions through audio-visual recordings and research, while recognising community storytellers and knowledge holders as custodians of tribal literary heritage.
Oral Traditions in Multilingual Education
The next session examined the role of indigenous languages and community knowledge in strengthening inclusive education. Moderated by Dr. K. Srinivasa Rao, former Secretary, Sahitya Akademi, the session featured Shri Anil Kumar Boro, Shri Sylvanus Lamare and Smt. Parvati Tirkey. The deliberations highlighted how oral narratives, traditional songs and community stories can enrich learning experiences and strengthen children’s connections with their mother tongues and cultural identities. The speakers emphasised incorporating indigenous knowledge and oral traditions into educational processes, particularly in early childhood education, and discussed the role of documentation, translation and technology in supporting tribal languages.
Emerging Writers and Poets Bring Contemporary Tribal Experiences to the Fore
The final two sessions provided a platform for tribal writers and poets to showcase their creative works and share contemporary narratives rooted in their linguistic and cultural identities. In the story-reading session, chaired by Shri Mahadev Toppo, Smt. Neeta Kusum Bilung, Shri Ramesh Karthik Nayak and Shri Vasanth Kumar V.P. presented their stories, highlighting the diversity of tribal literary expression and the evolving experiences of tribal communities.
The poetry-reading session, moderated by Smt. Jogamaya Chakma, brought together poets representing diverse linguistic and cultural traditions. Shri K. Vasamalli, Shri Kriri Mog Chowdhury, Shri Babu Sangda, Shri Hirjir Ingti Katharpi, Shri Gopi Krishna Soni, Smt. Marina Ekka, Smt. Sudha Chauhan and Smt. Anjali Belagal recited their original compositions. The readings reflected the richness of tribal poetry and its engagement with community life, cultural memory, identity and contemporary social realities.
Expanding Recognition and Reach of Tribal Literature
During the valedictory session, Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, emphasised the need to create sustainable platforms for promoting tribal literature, supporting authors writing in indigenous languages and connecting them with publishers and wider readerships. She highlighted
Living Roots Originals
, an initiative developed in collaboration with the Indian Performing Right Society (IPRS) to recognise and protect the creative rights of tribal musicians and performers. She also highlighted the Ministry’s initiative to facilitate a dedicated section for tribal literature at the National Book Trust’s forthcoming book fair at Pragati Maidan, providing tribal authors and publishers an opportunity to showcase their works and reach wider audiences.
Dr. K. Srinivasa Rao summarised the two-day festival, highlighting the representation of 27 languages, including 23 tribal languages. He emphasised that tribal literature is an integral part of India’s cultural heritage and underscored the need for its greater inclusion in university curricula, translation initiatives and mainstream publishing platforms to ensure wider recognition and dissemination.
In his concluding remarks, Shri Ganesh Nagarajan, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, highlighted the significant expansion of the Ministry’s cultural, linguistic and livelihood initiatives over the past year. He expressed appreciation to the scholars, authors, poets, moderators and participants for their valuable contributions to the festival.
In line with the Prime Minister’s vision of inclusive development and guided by the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat’ and ‘Vikas bhi, Virasat bhi’, the National Tribal Literary Festival reaffirmed the Ministry of Tribal Affairs’ commitment to bringing indigenous literary voices into the national discourse and ensuring that India’s tribal literary heritage remains an integral part of the journey towards Viksit Bharat@2047.

title: NSS organises block-level sports meets across the country to mobilise youth against substance abuse
subtitle: Week 9 of ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’ campaign witnesses participation of over 87,000 youth and community members across more than 130 institutions
ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, through the Directorate of MY Bharat-National Service Scheme (NSS), organised Cluster of Block-Level Sports Meets across the country under Week 9 of the 100-Week ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan’. Held under Month 3 of the campaign, themed ‘Strong Communities, Healthy Youth’, the initiative brought together thousands of student volunteers, local youth clubs and community members from neighbouring villages, blocks and colleges to promote discipline, teamwork and an addiction-free lifestyle through sports. A total of 992 activities were organised, mobilising 87,481 student volunteers, local youth club members and community spectators across the country.
Launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 02.08.2026 under the umbrella of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat campaign aims to promote a drug-free and healthy society by encouraging young people to stay away from drugs, alcohol, tobacco and other addictive substances.
Field reports from more than 130 institutions across 10 Regional Directorates – Bengaluru, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Chennai, Delhi, Guwahati, Jaipur, Lucknow and Trivandrum – included a range of sporting activities, including 100-metre and 400-metre sprints, marathons, Kabaddi, Kho-Kho, Volleyball, Football and Basketball. Traditional games such as Tug of War (Rassa-Kassi), Rumal Jhapat and Lemon Races were also organised. In Lakshadweep, participants took part in traditional island games organised under Regional Directorate Trivandrum.
The campaign also placed emphasis on gender inclusion, with 42,190 female participants taking part in sporting events and awareness activities. The sporting events were integrated with anti-addiction awareness activities to reinforce the message of the campaign. Each competition commenced with a collective Nasha Mukt Sankalp, with athletes, referees, coaches and spectators taking a pledge to uphold fair play and lead an addiction-free lifestyle.
Health awareness kiosks were set up at major clusters across Bhopal, Punjab, Rajasthan and Delhi. These kiosks disseminated Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials on mental health and provided information about the national de-addiction helpline (14446). The events were further supplemented by Nukkad Nataks (street plays), anti-drug rallies and slogan-writing competitions to raise awareness about substance abuse, peer pressure and pathways to recovery.
Local administration and specialists also extended support to the initiative. Senior police and Narcotics Cell officers from Bathinda, Kasaragod and Coimbatore, psychiatrists, de-addiction specialists and local civic representatives, including Panchayat Sarpanches, participated in the activities.

title: India’s Export Growth in FY 2026-27: Strong Performance, New Milestones
subtitle: Exports Record Seven Consecutive Months of Year-on-Year Growth

content:
India’s exports grew 16.66% to US$ 568.84 billion during April-October FY 2026-27, with gains across products, services and overseas markets. Export promotion measures, expanding trade partnerships and improved logistics are helping Indian businesses sustain this momentum. This growth complements India’s broader economic progress, marked by 7.8% GDP growth in April-June and unemployment declining to 5.1% in July-September. Major international organisations also reinforce this positive picture, projecting continued strong growth for FY 2026-27.
Introduction
International trade enables businesses to grow beyond domestic markets, supporting productivity and long-term economic development.  For India, exports have been an important contributor to economic growth, helping sustain expansion despite global headwinds.
This progress has sustained over several years. After reaching a new high in
FY 2021-22
, India’s total exports set fresh records in each successive financial year.  By
FY 2025-26
, they had reached
US$ 863.1 billion
, completing five consecutive years of record exports.
This momentum has continued into
FY 2026-27
, with
higher export values and growth
across a range of products and overseas markets.
India’s Export Growth Continues in FY 2026-27
Total exports are estimated at US$ 568.84 billion during April-October FY 2026-27
, up
16.66%
from US$ 487.59 billion a year earlier. The increase reflected growth in both merchandise and services exports.
Merchandise exports recorded
21.96%
growth during the period, whereas, services exports recorded
10.93%
growth.
Exports Recorded Positive Growth Every Month of FY 2026-27
The strength of this performance is sustained across the first half of FY 2026-27. Total exports reached
record US$ 479.0 billion during April-September FY 2026-27
. Merchandise and services exports also achieved
their highest-ever values for this period
.
Merchandise exports
reached
US$ 259.71 billion
, registering
18.4% year-on-year growth
.

reached
US$ 219.27 billion
, registering
10.2% year-on-year growth
.

, with total exports estimated at
US$ 89.99 billion
, registering
29.90% year-on-year growth
.

45.06% to US$ 49.47 billion.
Services exports were estimated at

Y-o-Y growth.
Broad-Based Sectoral Growth in India’s Exports
Services Remain a Strong Pillar of India’s Exports:
India’s services exports have expanded faster than the global average over the past decade. Services exports have helped
cushion India’s external sector
against geopolitical disruptions, reducing vulnerabilities and supporting trade stability.
Between 2015 and 2025, they grew at a compound annual rate of 10.3%, compared with 6.6% globally. Consequently, India’s share of global services exports increased from 3.1% to
4.3%.
During April-October FY 2026-27, they accounted for
~45.7%
of total exports.
India’s growing network of trade agreements is
widening access
to overseas markets for its services sector. These agreements
ease professional mobility
and
open opportunities
for Indian providers across diverse services.
Strong Sectoral Gains Support India’s Export Momentum:
India’s merchandise export growth drew strength from industrial goods as well as agricultural and traditional products. During April-October FY 2026-27,
seven of the ten leading export categories recorded double-digit growth.

Exports Strengthened Across Trade Agreement Partners

Regional partnerships recorded strong growth
, with exports to

The expansion extended to other long-standing partners

Export Performance Across Recent Trade Agreements
:

,
with exports growing

With India EU FTA coming into force early next year, Indian exports are all set to gain competitive advantage in a large trading block.
Exports within India’s Broader Economic Progress
India’s export growth complements the country’s broader economic progress, alongside strong domestic demand, improving employment conditions and a resilient external position.
A Strong Domestic Base
Real GDP grew
7.8% year-on-year in April-June FY 2026-27
, while the outlook for the financial year remains strong. The
Reserve Bank of India, OECD, IMF and World Bank project growth of 7-7.1%
, highlighting consumption, investment, exports and services as key drivers of economic momentum.
To read more about India’s GDP Performance in Q1 2026-27, please refer to

Poverty Reduction Over the Years
India’s economic progress is also reflected in falling poverty. According to the World Bank’s
Poverty & Equity Brief
(October 2026), the share of Indians living on less than
US$ 4.20 a day
fell from
57.7% in 2011 to 16.1% in 2023
, bringing about
496 million people out of poverty
. Over the same period, extreme poverty, i.e., living on less than

Women’s Participation Takes a Step Forward:

The improvement therefore extends beyond lower unemployment, with more people participating in the labour market and a greater proportion employed.
FDI Inflows and Forex Reserves
India’s external position also benefits from continued direct investment inflows and substantial reserves. Net foreign direct investment inflows rose to

Policy Support Sustaining India’s Export Momentum
Legal Foundation of India’s Foreign Trade
The Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992 provides
India’s legal framework for foreign trade.
India’s export policy supports businesses through duty relief, production support, local export development and targeted assistance. The
Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2023
, effective from 1 April 2023, provides the overarching framework for India’s exports and imports. The accompanying
Handbook of Procedures (HBP)
explains how its provisions are implemented.
Shaping Export Competitiveness
Supporting export production
FTP instruments facilitate access to inputs and equipment used in export production :

Broadening export participation: Taking Local Enterprises Global
Various policy and facilitation measures have been undertaken to support exports by MSMEs, startups, artisans and small exporters.
Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) :
The DEH initiative makes each district a unit of export planning, helping local enterprises build competitiveness and access global markets. Aligned with

E-Commerce Exports:
The FTP provides a framework for cross-border trade of goods and services in the digital economy, promoting e-commerce and emerging export channels. One such framework envisages
E-Commerce Export Hubs (ECEHs)
as centres providing business infrastructure and facilities for cross-border e-commerce.
Export Promotion Mission (EPM): An Integrated Push
Approved in
November
2025
,
EPM
has an outlay of
₹25,060 crore for FY 2025-26 to FY 2030-31
to strengthen export competitiveness, expand exports and generate employment. It combines financial and non-financial support across trade finance, compliance, market access and logistics. The Scheme focuses on
MSMEs, first-time exporters, labour-intensive sectors and exporters in interior and low-export regions
.
Support During Trade Disruptions:
The

supporting MSMEs.
The component provides covers for higher freight costs, insurance premiums and war-related risks from Gulf-West Asia maritime disruptions. It covers both eligible past shipments and prospective exports.
To read more on EPM, please refer to

Unlocking Overseas Markets: Rising Trade Partnerships
India’s expanding trade partnerships are widening market access and strengthening economic resilience amid global challenges.
The Evolving Landscape of India’s Trade Partnerships:
Alongside implementing recent agreements, India is pursuing

to expand its global reach. This includes talks with the

. Additionally, f

are also underway, including the

and

To read more on India’s Trade Partnerships, please refer to

Special Economic Zones (SEZs):

SEZs are designated areas that
promote trade and investment

Streamlining Export Delivery
India is strengthening export delivery through digital services, simpler customs procedures and better access to logistics infrastructure.
Trade Connect
is designed to empower Indian exporters by bringing international trade information and services into one place, easing access to global markets.

simplify postal exports through booking, digital documentation and customs clearance. As of January 2026,

These efforts are complemented by the

Conclusion
India’s recent export performance reflects growth in both merchandise and services, with gains extending across products and partner countries. This expansion draws on the
collective efforts
of exporters, MSMEs, traders and the government to strengthen competitiveness and reach new buyers. These efforts are backed by consistent policy support through manufacturing incentives, market-access assistance and logistics initiatives.
Additionally, measures to simplify trade, improve connectivity and help businesses enter new markets continue to reinforce this support. These measures will further support Indian enterprises to build their reach across wider markets.

title: Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission
subtitle: Unlocking India’s Tribal Forest Economy
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 8:55AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Many of India’s
10.4 crore Scheduled Tribes derive 20–40% of their annual income
from
Minor Forest Produce (MFP).
Historically, tribals sold this produce to middlemen at distress prices, earning below the cost of their own labour. To address this, the government runs the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM). The mission
organises tribals into community-owned Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs),
moving them from raw produce sellers to
value-adding entrepreneurs
. As of March 2026,
4,172 VDVKs
have been sanctioned
covering
12.48 lakh
beneficiaries. The government also buys MFP at a pre-determined Minimum Support Price (MSP). PMJVM provides enterprise funding and helps tribals access markets through fairs, e-commerce platforms, and exhibitions.
Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is observing
Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada
across the country from
1 to 15 November 2026
, culminating in
Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas on 15 November
, the birth anniversary of
Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda
. The Government of India designated 15 November as Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas in
2021
. The Pakhwada is a focused, time-bound drive to accelerate the Ministry’s flagship programmes and take their benefits to tribal families at the last mile. On Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas,
over 300 projects
for tribal communities across States will be taken up, with
228 ready for inauguration
and
74 for foundation stone laying
. Two national digital initiatives, the
Jan-HIT Portal
and the
National FRA Digital Platform
, will also be launched. Tribal Research Institutes have planned
more than 160 activities in 19 States/UTs
.
Click to Read More:
Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada 2026: Nationwide Celebrations to Honour Tribal Heritage, Empower Communities and Accelerate Last-Mile Delivery of Welfare Schemes
Protecting Tribal Forest Economies
For millions of forest-dwelling tribal families, Minor Forest Produce (MFP)—such as
honey, tendu leaves, mahua flowers, tamarind, lac, bamboo and wild herbs
—is not merely a forest resource. It is a primary source of livelihood. About
20% to 40% of their annual income
is from selling MFP. Yet, despite directly procuring and selling MFP, tribals receive only a fraction of its market value. This is because they often sell MFP to intermediaries at low prices.
The
Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM)
seeks to change this equation. Launched in 2021-22, the Mission provides a systematic way for them to improve MFP’s value by
skilling the tribals in newer technology and practices
. The scheme links the communities to the larger
national and digital markets
to help them get more exposure and sell more products. It also guarantees
Minimum Support Prices (MSP)
to tribals by directly procuring the produce from them.
These efforts are helping forest gatherers become owners of their community enterprises while strengthening India’s
tribal economy
at the grassroots level.
Minor Forest Products & Minimum Support Price
While the government manages most of India’s forests to preserve ecology and wildlife, tribals and other traditional forest-dwelling communities are given access to these areas for the preservation of their livelihoods.
In 2006, the government enacted the
Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act
— also called the
Forest Rights Act
. The Act defines minor forest produce as “
all non-timber forest produce of plant origin including bamboo, brush wood, stumps, cane, tussar, cocoons, honey, wax, lac, tendu or kendu leaves, medicinal plants and herbs, roots, tubers and the like
.” The government has
notified Minimum Support Price for 87 MFP items under PMJVM
.
The Forest Rights Act recognises that forest-dwelling communities have historically depended on forest products for sustenance and livelihood. The Act gives tribals
rights to procure and sell non-timber minor forest produce.
Separately, the Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act (1996) grants tribal Gram Panchayats ownership rights over minor forest produce.
The
Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED)
, mandated with the marketing and development of tribal products, purchases non-timber forest produce at the pre-determined price (MSP) regardless of the market price of the product. It does so through a network of state implementing agencies — including tribal development cooperatives and forest development corporations. Since 2013–14, state governments have
procured 2,67,954 metric tonnes of MFPs
worth
Rs. 693.98 crore
under the scheme.
How Does PMJVM Support Tribals?
Beyond MSP procurement, the PVJM scheme also provides skilling, technological, marketing, and infrastructural support to tribals.
Organising Tribals into Van Dhan Vikas Kendras
The Mission mobilises tribal gatherers into self-help groups (SHGs). A
group of 15 SHGs, comprising about 300 tribals
, are clustered together into one Van Dhan Vikas Kendra (VDVK). At least 60% of VDVK members must be from Scheduled Tribe communities.
The
Van Dhan Yojana
, launched on April 14, 2018, is a part of PMJVM. It forms the foundation of the VDVK model and powers its implementation across tribal communities.
Skilling, Funding and Technological Support
The Government organises skilling and other training programmes for MFP gatherers, including trainings on scientific harvesting practices, at Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs).
The SHGs are also provided with:
Infrastructural support
, established in a beneficiary’s home or a government or gram panchayat building
Primary processing equipment
— cutting and sieving tools, decorticators, dryers, and packaging tools — based on locally available MFPs
Training
for 30 members on sustainable harvesting and value addition, with raw materials and trainee kits provided
Working capital
, facilitated through tie-ups with financial institutions, banks, and the National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC)
Storage and transportation
support on a rental basis.
Marketing and Business Support
Apart from value addition, VDVKs are also
centres for market linkages
– both local and distant – for the final products.
VDVKs are established around local Haat Bazaars
, the primary MFP procurement points, to make it easier for tribals to sell products they produce.
There are over
5,000 Haats in tribal areas
.
Haats are being
modernised
in a phased manner— with permanent structures, storage, drinking water, shade, and weighing equipment.
VDVKs
may partner with private entities or non-profits for value addition or marketing of their products.
TRIFED
disseminates market intelligence — including daily rates and e-commerce avenues —to VDVKs to improve their decision-making on business deals.
PMJVM also provides:
Branding, promotion, and advertisement of tribal products through festivals, exhibitions, and artisan melas
Geo-tagging of VDVKs and other scheme assets
Geographical Indicators for tribal produce (GI is a sign used on products that have a specific geographical origin and possess qualities or a reputation that are due to that origin)
Building and upgrading IT and e-commerce platforms
Research and development support
Under the PMJVM scheme:
4,172 VDVKs have been sanctioned
and
2,911 VDVKs are functional
, with reported
sales of around Rs. 168 crores
(as on July 31, 2026).
12.48 lakh tribal members
have been linked to the VDVKs.
VDVKs Help in Tribal Women Empowerment
Most collections and sales are carried out by women, making PMJVM a key instrument of tribal women’s financial empowerment.
The
Nyigamane, Ho Yorbe, Medumhagdum VDVK
in
Arunachal Pradesh
’s Leparada district was established in October 2021 with
300 women SHG members and farmers
. This VDVK converts locally available non-timber forest and agricultural produce into processed, marketable goods. The products created are:
King Chilli Pickle
from King Chillis (Bhut Jolokia — a north eastern Indian specialty)
Bamboo Shoot Pickle
from bamboo shoots (a common MFP in north-eastern India)
Turmeric Powder
from locally grown turmeric
Ginger Powder
from locally grown ginger
Pineapple Jam
from Pineapples (abundant in Arunachal Pradesh)
Pineapple Squash
from Pineapples
Orange Squash
from Oranges
The VDVK has
sold Rs. 11 lakh worth of these products from 2022-23
onwards. It has empowered the women, who no longer need to depend on only seasonable agriculture for income throughout the year. The women jointly own the business – they are not mere workers but also have a stake in the brand and the enterprise.
Towards A Sustainable Forest Economy
Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) provides livelihood opportunities to forest-dwelling tribals, offering a systematic way to produce and market non-timber forest produce. These products are locally sourced and rooted in traditional practices — representing a forest-based economy
balancing community ownership with market competitiveness.
In a world increasingly driven by mass-manufactured and plastic-packaged goods, they are India’s distinctive offering:
natural, community-owned, and forest-born
. PMJVM embodies
Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikaas
- ensuring India’s growth story reaches its most remote forests and the communities who call them home. This will eventually contribute to India’s vision of a
Viksit Bharat@2047
.

title: CCI approves acquisition of certain shareholding of Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Limited by Rasmalai Limited
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 NOV 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved the acquisition of certain shareholding of Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd. by Rasmalai Limited.
The proposed combination relates to acquisition of certain shareholding by Rasmalai Limited (
Acquirer
) in Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Limited (
Target
).
The Acquirer is an entity incorporated in Cyprus with the principal activity of holding investments and currently has no activities or presence in India. The Acquirer is indirectly controlled by investment funds managed and/or advised by Advent International, L.P. and/or its affiliates.
The Target operates a network of super-specialty hospitals in India, providing comprehensive healthcare services, diagnostics, and advanced medical procedures across multiple specialties.
